set.body:
Current milestone assessment

Sequential assessment 2026-09-12: retain P1 as an aggregate scientific-identity milestone. Live graph records phases 0..3 closed and Phase 4 open; P4.4 owns the remaining release evidence refresh. Current FmriModel carries design schema/row-layout/fingerprint access and structural hypothesis suites remain present, so do not restart the architecture from the historical 245531a review. This assessment does not claim every structural contract requalified: final closure must map the original global acceptance to current public APIs, scenario construction, fixtures and clean-candidate receipts. Historical coordination targets for the old fit architecture and result bundles are now retired/closed; durable output work is owned by bd-01KX6G9B8R86MRBZ9S8K8F5G7V and existing estimates modules, not another result hierarchy. Keep rendered labels non-authoritative, portable shared code and Gale ownership. Avoid broad scope expansion into every later optional modeling feature; evaluate the originally adopted identity contract and explicitly record any current violation rather than silently assuming closed phases still prove it.

Retained original acceptance

Objective

Make scientific identity load-bearing across hrf, design, model, fit, and hypothesis evaluation. Compilation may lower events and bases to matrices, but term, cell, modulation, basis, run, row-layout, and policy meaning must remain inspectable and machine-checkable through fit results and inference.

Review basis

This epic is grounded in the live design-hardening source review at 245531a. It evolves EventModel, DesignBlock, FmriModel, FitPlan, compiled contrasts, and existing results; it must not introduce a parallel analysis stack merely to match an external proposal.

Permanent constraints

- Preserve the current hrf -> design -> model -> fit dependency direction.
- Keep shared production code portable across JVM and Scala.js.
- Reuse Gale and existing linalg capabilities; no domain-local solver family.
- Preserve rendered names as presentation and compatibility data, never as the sole scientific authority.
- Keep runtime BIDS/DataTable compilation canonical. The closed decision bd-01KYYM0W2VTVT4VBSYK9HYFXZG remains in force: no formula macro and no schema-typed DataTable without new evidence.
- Coordinate with, but do not duplicate, fit architecture bd-01KX2CPJYP0DP751T841N00V6E, typed result bundles bd-01KX2CQZHGH43S93RK1KCY7ES1, and out-of-core preparation bd-01KX6G9B1ZT10A3214DPA096RZ.

Global acceptance criteria

- [ ] Every realized design column has one stable structural origin containing the scientifically relevant term, cell, modulator, basis, role, and run scope.
- [ ] Matrix, row layout, structural column schema, audit, and deterministic design fingerprint remain inseparable through the model boundary.
- [ ] A compiled hypothesis is bound to the intended design fingerprint and structural column identities and fails before evaluation on a different design.
- [ ] Coefficient hypotheses, basis omnibus tests, and linear response functionals are explicit and unambiguous.
- [ ] Factor levels, empty cells, missing modulators, centering, weighting, rank, censoring, and run coefficient scope have inspectable policies and receipts.
- [ ] The public DMS workflow constructs and tests the expected 50 task columns without manual table explosion, column offsets, name parsing, or numeric contrast bookkeeping.
- [ ] Each accepted capability has JVM and Scala.js tests, suitable algebraic or metamorphic checks, and independent numerical evidence where parity is claimed.
- [ ] Scenario manifests, fixture receipts, external generators, CI gates, documentation, and performance claims agree with the implemented public surface.
- [ ] Full focused module gates and ultimately compileAll/testAll are warning-clean before epic closure.

Phases

0. Repair the evidence boundary and scenario court.
1. Carry structural scientific identity through compilation and inference.
2. Make design policies and missing fit semantics explicit.
3. Prove flagship scientific workflows.
4. Close the computational assurance and release court.
